species.name: Lake trout
why: Water 52°F on top, right in their comfort range.
Best water today is 12–46 ft deep, mostly on channel edges.
The lake is layered: warm water down to about 50 ft, cold below.
Little oxygen below about 80 ft, so fish stay above it.

species.name: Trout
why: Water 52°F on top, a bit cool for them, so they feed in the warmest water they can find.
Best water today is 14–26 ft deep, mostly on channel edges.
The lake is layered: warm water down to about 50 ft, cold below.
Little oxygen below about 80 ft, so fish stay above it.

species.name: Yellow perch
why: Water 52°F on top, much colder than they like, so they move slowly and stay deep.
Best water today is 8–34 ft deep, mostly on wind-blown banks.
The lake is layered: warm water down to about 50 ft, cold below.
Little oxygen below about 80 ft, so fish stay above it.

species.name: Smallmouth bass
why: Water 52°F on top, much colder than they like, so they move slowly and stay deep.
Best water today is 6–30 ft deep, mostly on wind-blown banks.
The lake is layered: warm water down to about 50 ft, cold below.
Little oxygen below about 80 ft, so fish stay above it.
Northwest wind at 9 mph pushes bait onto the southeast shore: try the wind-blown banks.
